steps.title: A new look at what a dry spell really costs
steps.narration: Every certified claim on the Evidence page now includes a plain-language breakdown of what following it has historically felt like to hold, split out by the market phase you'd have entered in.
steps.point_out: Below each card's existing details, a new panel appears headed 'Historical drawdown & dry-spell expectations,' with one row per market phase — Expansion, Pullback, Correction, Bear, and Recovery. The green 'GO' banner at the top still confirms today's board is current.

steps.title: Real figures, not vague warnings
steps.narration: Where there's plenty of history to draw on, the panel shows real numbers: how deep the typical drawdown ran, how long positions stayed underwater, and how long recovery usually took — each labeled with its own sample size.
steps.point_out: The first card's Expansion row shows a median max-drawdown of -7.70% (90th-percentile -3.72%) across 1,264 observations.

steps.title: Honest when one measure runs thin
steps.narration: When a single measure doesn't have enough history behind it, the panel says so plainly instead of guessing — while its neighboring measures still show real figures.
steps.point_out: On the same card, the Correction row's 'Longest losing streak' cell reads 'insufficient (n=5)' in muted gray, even though the row's other three measures are real, well-populated numbers.

steps.title: Even a whole empty phase is shown honestly
steps.narration: For a claim whose history has zero examples in a given phase, every measure in that row admits it — never a fabricated number or a broken card.
steps.point_out: The second claim card's Correction and Bear rows both read 'insufficient (n=0)' across all four measures, while the rest of that same card renders normally around them.

steps.title: The method is explained, not hidden
steps.narration: Two short sentences under every table spell out exactly how the numbers are counted and remind readers this is history, not a promise.
steps.point_out: The same two sentences appear word-for-word under every one of the seven cards, ending with 'Read the edge as an upper bound, not a guarantee.'

expect.text: Walk-forward evidence now spans up to ~30 years of history

steps.title: The leaderboard looks exactly as before
steps.narration: Away from the Evidence page, nothing else changed — the stock leaderboard still marks every score honestly.
steps.point_out: Every Leadership, Entry Quality, and Risk score still carries a small 'Not yet proven' badge, since no claim has passed certification yet.

steps.title: A single stock's page is untouched too
steps.narration: A stock's own page still shows the same three honestly-labeled scores, with no drill-down control appearing where none is warranted.
steps.point_out: All three score cards on AAPL's page read 'Not yet proven,' and there's still no 'Why proven?' button, since nothing here is certified yet.

steps.title: Deep price history still expands on demand
steps.narration: The button that loads a stock's full multi-decade trading history still works exactly as before.
steps.point_out: Clicking 'Full history' grows the chart from about five years of bars to nearly thirty, adding a note that the older bars are weekly-sampled.

steps.title: The Data Manager page is unaffected
steps.narration: The page for growing and checking the dataset still loads cleanly, with its coverage details intact.
steps.point_out: The 'Dataset coverage' panel still lists price history, universe size, and backfill gaps — nothing about it changed.
